blindSummary:
This country is the most progressive destination in its region for transgender visitors: there is no criminalisation, anti-discrimination protections exist, legal gender recognition runs through the courts (with dead-name removal from identity documents from 2025), transition-related healthcare is publicly funded, and one of its coastal cities is a queer hub for the whole region.

Two traveller-specific risks pull against this. First, its main international airport has no regulations for interacting with trans travellers - documented humiliating questioning and detainment, with surgery demanded for gender recognition ("If you don't undergo surgery, you're still a male"); every foreign visitor transits this airport, making it a high-probability friction point. Second, violence is rising sharply: 433 homophobic/transphobic physical incidents were reported in 2025, including dating-app traps and organized ambushes, with transgender people "bearing the brunt". Anti-trans rhetoric from the leadership of a large allied state is reportedly inflaming the local climate.

The right-wing governing coalition and the aftermath of an ongoing armed conflict have weakened protections, though parliament's security committee has convened on LGBTQ public-space safety.
blindOutOfScope: Security risks from the ongoing armed conflict (rockets, terrorism, border areas) affect all travellers; only trans-specific risk is assessed here.
blindSourceSummaries: A magazine feature (May 2023) on trans people's ordeal at this country's airports: the national airport operator has no rules for interacting with trans travellers; trans people describe humiliating questioning and detention at the main international airport ('If you don't undergo surgery, you're still a male'). Directly documents airport-screening problems for trans travellers here.

National newspaper (May 2026): the national LGBTQ organisation's 2025 annual report found 432 homophobic or transphobic physical incidents in this country in 2025 - a sharp rise, including carefully planned ambush attacks arranged through dating apps, stabbings and extortion.

News site (May 2026): the country's 2025 report on anti-LGBTQ violence finds record-high levels - at least one physical assault per week; physical attacks rose to half of public-space incidents (from 32%); extortion/threats rose from 3% to 13.5%; 91% of survey respondents experienced anti-LGBTQ hostility in the past year but only 7% reported it; trans people bear the brunt despite being a minority within the community.

National newspaper (Feb 2025): anti-trans rhetoric and executive orders from the leadership of a large allied state are affecting this country's transgender community - activists report increasing violent rhetoric locally, including transphobia from within the LGBTQ community.

National newspaper (May 2023): the national police issued a new regulation for body searches of trans people who have not fully transitioned - male officers will search male genitalia and female officers female genitalia; LGBTQ groups decry the regulation as harmful, humiliating and traumatic (previously officers had to ask the person's preference).

National newspaper (June 2024): the interior ministry amended ID regulations so trans people no longer need to register their 'dead name' on their identity card - following a high-court petition by a trans woman who argued that displaying the previous name outed her gender change.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404 - page removed); the underlying page addressed trans rights in this country - laws, protections and gaps.

International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): no criminalisation since the 1988 repeal; anti-discrimination protections across statutes (a 2000 equal-services law, a patient-rights law, a student-rights law - the latter also covering gender identity); conversion practices prohibited for medical professionals; same-sex marriages performed abroad registrable since 2006; joint adoption affirmed by the high court in 2018.

National news site: a broadcaster's survey found majority public support for same-sex marriage while half of lawmakers declined to state a position, including a culture minister who has marched in the pride parade.
blindLocalsOnly: Court-based legal gender recognition with dead-name removal (2025) and publicly funded transition healthcare are resident-facing.
blindTangential: Dating-app traps and organized ambushes are a direct caution for trans visitors using apps.
